claim: Production of proliferative follicle cells (FCs) and quiescent escort cells (ECs) by follicle stem cells (FSCs) in adult Drosophila ovaries is regulated by niche signals from anterior (cap cells, ECs) and posterior (polar FCs) sources.
source: Production of proliferative follicle cells (FCs) and quiescent escort cells (ECs) by follicle stem cells (FSCs) in adult Drosophila ovaries is regulated by niche signals from anterior (cap cells, ECs) and posterior (polar FCs) sources.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior work and is presented as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: ECs, FSCs, and FCs develop from common pupal precursors.
source: Here we show that ECs, FSCs, and FCs develop from common pupal precursors, with different fates acquired by progressive separation of cells along the AP axis and a graded decline in anterior cell proliferation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by lineage tracing experiments and morphological observations described throughout the manuscript.

claim: Different fates of ECs, FSCs, and FCs are acquired by progressive separation of cells along the AP axis.
source: Here we show that ECs, FSCs, and FCs develop from common pupal precursors, with different fates acquired by progressive separation of cells along the AP axis and a graded decline in anterior cell proliferation.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by lineage tracing data showing AP clustering of marked cells and morphological studies.

claim: There is a graded decline in anterior cell proliferation during pupal development.
source: Here we show that ECs, FSCs, and FCs develop from common pupal precursors, with different fates acquired by progressive separation of cells along the AP axis and a graded decline in anterior cell proliferation.
evidence: This is supported by EdU labeling, FUCCI analysis, and lineage tracing data showing reduced proliferation in anterior regions over time.

claim: ECs, FSCs, and most FCs derive from intermingled cell (IC) precursors interspersed with germline cells.
source: ECs, FSCs, and most FCs derive from intermingled cell (IC) precursors interspersed with germline cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by lineage tracing and morphological observations showing that ICs give rise to these cell types.

claim: Precursors accumulate posterior to ICs before engulfing a naked germline cyst projected out of the germarium to form the first egg chamber.
source: Precursors also accumulate posterior to ICs before engulfing a naked germline cyst projected out of the germarium to form the first egg chamber and posterior polar FC signaling center.
evidence: This is supported by live imaging and fixed morphological observations showing EGC and basal stalk cells enveloping the first germline cyst.

claim: Stem and niche cells develop in appropriate numbers and spatial organization through regulated proliferative expansion together with progressive establishment of spatial signaling cues.
source: Thus, stem and niche cells develop in appropriate numbers and spatial organization through regulated proliferative expansion together with progressive establishment of spatial signaling cues that guide adult cell behavior, rather than through rigid early specification events.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the collective data showing gradual fate acquisition rather than early specification.

claim: Adult stem cells generally act as a community, coordinating the activities of multiple individual cells to replenish tissues throughout life.
source: Adult stem cells generally act as a community, coordinating the activities of multiple individual cells to replenish tissues throughout life (Clevers and Watt, 2018; Post and Clevers, 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to prior literature and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: Adult stem cell behavior is invariably regulated by external signals from other cell types, known as niche cells.
source: Their behavior is invariably regulated by external signals from other cell types, known as niche cells (Biteau et al., 2011; Losick et al., 2011; Voog and Jones, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and represents established knowledge.

claim: It is essential to establish adult stem cells in suitable numbers and niche environments during development to ensure appropriately regulated community activity in adults.
source: It is therefore essential to establish adult stem cells in suitable numbers and niche environments during development to ensure appropriately regulated community activity in adults.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the established role of niche cells in regulating stem cell behavior.

claim: The development of terminally differentiated adult cell types commonly results from a series of successive, definitive, and largely irreversible decisions.
source: The development of terminally differentiated adult cell types commonly results from a series of successive, definitive, and largely irreversible decisions that are stabilized by potentially long-lasting shifts in gene expression and chromatin modification (Adam and Harwell, 2020; Davidson et al., 2002; Rothman and Jarriault, 2019; Sagner and Briscoe, 2019; Salinas et al., 2020; Zechner et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations and represents established knowledge about cell differentiation.

claim: Stem cells typically continue to proliferate in adulthood and often exhibit malleable relationships with their products.
source: First, stem cells typically continue to proliferate in adulthood and often exhibit malleable relationships with their products, with the potential for marked changes in inter-conversion rates in either direction (Donati and Watt, 2015; Tetteh et al., 2015; Wabik and Jones, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature describing stem cell behavior.

claim: Drosophila ovarian follicle stem cells (FSCs) present a particularly interesting and experimentally favorable paradigm to investigate stem cell development.
source: Drosophila ovarian follicle stem cells (FSCs) present a particularly interesting and experimentally favorable paradigm to investigate because the organization, behavior, and regulation of these adult stem cells have been studied thoroughly, revealing many similarities to the important mammalian paradigm of gut stem cells (Gehart and Clevers, 2019; Hayashi et al., 2020; Reilein et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations showing prior characterization of FSCs and their similarity to mammalian gut stem cells.

claim: FSCs directly produce two different types of cell in adult ovaries: follicle cells (FCs) and escort cells (ECs).
source: FSCs directly produce two different types of cell in adult ovaries, follicle cells (FCs) and escort cells (ECs) (Reilein et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work characterizing FSC behavior.

claim: Both FCs and ECs act as niche cells, producing key JAK-STAT and Wnt signals, respectively.
source: Both of these cell types also act as niche cells, producing key JAK-STAT and Wnt signals, respectively (Reilein et al., 2017; Melamed and Kalderon, 2020; Song and Xie, 2003; Vied et al., 2012; Waghmare and Page-McCaw, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work characterizing signaling from these cell types.

claim: Paneth cells in the mammalian small intestine are both stem cell products and niche cells.
source: Similarly, Paneth cells in the mammalian small intestine are both stem cell products and niche cells (Beumer and Clevers, 2020; Hsu and Fuchs, 2012; Fuchs and Blau, 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature on mammalian gut stem cells.

claim: GSCs and FSCs are housed in the germarium, which is the most anterior region of each ovariole.
source: GSCs and FSCs are housed in the germarium, which is the most anterior region of each of the 30–40 ovarioles comprising the adult ovary (Figure 1A; Hayashi et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation and reference to Figure 1A showing germarium structure.

claim: Somatic terminal filament (TF) and cap cells at the anterior of the germarium are stable sources of niche signals for GSCs and FSCs.
source: Somatic terminal filament (TF) and cap cells at the anterior of the germarium are stable sources of niche signals for GSCs and FSCs, including bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs), Hedgehog, and Wnt proteins, with GSCs directly contacting cap cells (Hayashi et al., 2020; Kahney et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work characterizing niche signals in the germarium.

claim: Cystoblast daughters of GSCs divide four times with incomplete cytokinesis to yield a progression of 2-, 4-, 8-, and finally, 16-cell germline cysts.
source: Cystoblast daughters of GSCs divide four times with incomplete cytokinesis to yield a progression of 2-, 4-, 8-, and finally, 16-cell germline cysts.
evidence: This is established knowledge about germline development, supported by observations in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Germline cyst maturation is accompanied by posterior movement and depends on interactions with neighboring quiescent, somatic ECs.
source: Their maturation is accompanied by posterior movement and depends on interactions with neighboring quiescent, somatic ECs (Kirilly et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work on germline-EC interactions.

claim: ECs act as niche cells for adjacent or nearby GSCs and FSCs.
source: ECs also act as niche cells for adjacent or nearby GSCs and FSCs (Hayashi et al., 2020; Waghmare and Page-McCaw, 2018; Sahai-Hernandez and Nystul, 2013; Wang and Page-McCaw, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work on EC function.

claim: A rounded stage 2a 16-cell cyst loses EC contacts as it forms a lens-shaped stage 2b cyst spanning the width of the germarium.
source: A rounded stage 2a 16-cell cyst loses EC contacts as it forms a lens-shaped stage 2b cyst spanning the width of the germarium and subsequently recruits FCs (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the morphological progression of germline cysts, illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The earliest FCs can be recognized by expression of high levels of the surface adhesion protein, Fasciclin 3 (Fas3).
source: The earliest FCs can be recognized by expression of high levels of the surface adhesion protein, Fasciclin 3 (Fas3) (Reilein et al., 2017; Zhang and Kalderon, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work characterizing FC markers.

claim: Polar cells produce the JAK-STAT ligand, Unpaired, which patterns the development of FCs along the anterior-posterior (AP) axis of each developing egg chamber.
source: Polar cells produce the JAK-STAT ligand, Unpaired, which patterns the development of FCs along the anterior-posterior (AP) axis of each developing egg chamber (Duhart et al., 2017; McGregor et al., 2002; Xi et al., 2003) and creates a gradient of signaling activity across the FSC domain, which is critical for FSC divisions and for FSC conversion to FCs (Melamed and Kalderon, 2020; Vied et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work on JAK-STAT signaling in the ovary.

claim: There are about 16 FSCs that reside in three rings or layers around the inner germarial surface between ECs and FCs on the AP axis.
source: There are about 16 FSCs that reside in three rings or layers around the inner germarial surface between ECs and FCs on the AP axis (Figure 1A; Hayashi et al., 2020; Reilein et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: The most posterior FSCs directly become FCs, while anterior FSCs directly become ECs.
source: The most posterior FSCs directly become FCs, while anterior FSCs directly become ECs, but FSCs also exchange AP locations, allowing a single FSC lineage to include both ECs and FCs (Reilein et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior lineage tracing work.

claim: FSCs exchange AP locations, allowing a single FSC lineage to include both ECs and FCs.
source: The most posterior FSCs directly become FCs, while anterior FSCs directly become ECs, but FSCs also exchange AP locations, allowing a single FSC lineage to include both ECs and FCs (Reilein et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior lineage tracing work.

claim: Individual FSCs are frequently lost and frequently amplify, with no evident temporal or functional link between division and differentiation.
source: Individual FSCs are frequently lost and frequently amplify, with no evident temporal or functional link between division and differentiation (Reilein et al., 2018b), so that the representation and output (of ECs and FCs) of any one FSC lineage is highly variable (Reilein et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on FSC dynamics.

claim: All FSC behaviors are largely regulated by extracellular signals that are graded along the AP axis.
source: All of these behaviors are largely regulated by extracellular signals that are graded along the AP axis, with especially prominent roles for JAK-STAT ligand derived from polar cells and Wnt ligands derived from both cap cells and ECs (Reilein et al., 2017; Melamed and Kalderon, 2020; Song and Xie, 2003; Vied and Kalderon, 2009; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work on signaling regulation of FSCs.

claim: The number of FSCs, together with the spatially regulated signals that guide division rate, is matched to steady-state production of 5–6 FCs every 12 hr.
source: The number of FSCs, together with the spatially regulated signals that guide division rate, is matched to steady-state production of 5–6 FCs every 12 hr (Reilein et al., 2018b), while the number and location of ECs is important not only to deliver some niche signals directly but may also be important to keep FSCs at a suitable distance from the cap cell source of Wnt and Hh signals.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior quantitative work on FSC output.

claim: At 0 hr APF, ovaries are not yet organized into distinct germaria.
source: (B) At 0 hr APF, ovaries are not yet organized into distinct germaria.
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1B showing ovary morphology at 0 hr APF.

claim: Individual germline cells are intermingled with somatic IC precursor cells at 0 hr APF.
source: Individual germline cells (green) are intermingled with somatic IC precursor cells (white).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1B.

claim: At 12 hr APF, ovaries are organized into distinct germaria, separated by a layer of migrating apical cells.
source: (C) At 12 hr APF, ovaries are organized into distinct germaria, separated by a layer of migrating apical cells.
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1C showing ovary morphology at 12 hr APF.

claim: Lamin-C stains the nuclear envelope of TF cells.
source: Lamin-C stains the nuclear envelope of TF cells (cyan arrowhead).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1C showing Lamin-C staining pattern.

claim: Fas3 staining is present on the medial side of the ovariole at 12 hr APF.
source: Fas3 staining is present on the medial side of the ovariole (pink arrowhead).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1C showing Fas3 expression pattern.

claim: By 24 hr APF, Fas3 is spread more evenly around the circumference of the ovary.
source: (E) by 24 hr APF, Fas3 is spread more evenly around the circumference of the ovary, and stains a hub into which the posterior ends of nascent basal stalks converge.
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1E showing Fas3 expression pattern at 24 hr APF.

claim: By 48 hr APF, Fas3 begins to be expressed dimly in posterior ICs.
source: (H) By 48 hr APF, Fas3 begins to be expressed dimly in posterior ICs (yellow arrowhead) and Lamin-C expression (red) is clear in epithelial sheath cells (white arrowhead).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1H showing Fas3 expression pattern at 48 hr APF.

claim: At 56 hr APF, germaria begin to bud the first egg chamber.
source: (I) At 56 hr APF, germaria begin to bud the first egg chamber
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1I showing egg chamber budding.

claim: By 102 hr APF, 3–4 egg chambers have budded.
source: (J) by 102 hr APF, 3–4 egg chambers have budded.
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1J showing multiple budded egg chambers.

claim: At 0 hr APF, germline cells are single cells or two cell cysts.
source: (A–A'') At 0 hr APF, germline cells are single cells (cyan arrowheads) or two cell cysts (white arrowheads).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing germline cyst sizes.

claim: At 12 hr APF, the majority of germline cells have one or two cells, but posterior cysts may have four or eight cells.
source: (B–B'') At 12 hr APF, the majority of germline cells have one or two cells, but posterior cysts may have four (white arrow) or eight cells (cyan arrow).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 1B showing germline cyst progression.

claim: At 18 hr APF, longer germaria have 16 cells in posterior cysts, whereas short germaria have only 2 cells in posterior cysts.
source: (C–C'') At 18 hr APF, there is a large range of germarial length and corresponding posterior cyst maturity. Longer germaria have 16 cells in posterior cysts (yellow arrows), whereas short germaria have only 2 cells in posterior cysts (white arrowhead).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 1C showing variability in germline development.

claim: At 24 hr APF, the majority of germaria have 16 cells in posterior cysts.
source: (D–D'') At 24 hr APF, the majority of germaria have 16 cells in posterior cysts (yellow arrows) but the most posterior cyst has not yet moved beyond other cysts.
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 1D showing germline cyst maturation.

claim: By 48 hr APF, each germarium has a single most posterior 16-cell cyst.
source: (F–F'') By 48 hr APF, each germarium has a single most posterior 16-cell cyst.
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 1F showing germline organization.

claim: EdU labeling was seen in the most posterior germline cyst at 12 hr APF, 18 hr APF, and 24 hr APF.
source: (A–C) EdU (green) in the most posterior germline cyst (pink outlines) was seen at (A') 12 hr APF, (B) 18 hr APF, and (C') 24 hr APF.
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-C showing EdU incorporation in germline cysts.

claim: Somatic cells with EdU were observed among all intermingled cells (ICs) and at higher frequency in Fas3-positive cells posterior to the developing germarium from 12 to 24 hr APF.
source: (A–F) Somatic cells with (green) EdU (yellow arrows) were observed (A–C) among all intermingled cells (ICs) and at higher frequency in Fas3-positive cells posterior to the developing germarium from 12 to 24 hr APF.
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-C showing EdU incorporation patterns in somatic cells.

claim: ICs in the anterior third of the germarium were rarely labeled with EdU at 48 hr APF or later.
source: (D–F) ICs in the anterior third of the germarium were rarely labeled at 48 hr APF or later (green signals without yellow arrows are germline cells)
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 2D-F showing reduced EdU incorporation in anterior ICs.

claim: TJ-positive, Fas3-positive extra-germarial crown (EGC) cells were frequently labeled with EdU at 48 hr APF.
source: but (D, D') TJ-positive, Fas3-positive extra-germarial crown (EGC) cells were frequently labeled (white arrows)
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 2D showing EdU incorporation in EGC cells.

claim: A few ICs in the anterior half of the germarium were still labeled with EdU at 60 hr APF.
source: and (E, E') a few ICs in the anterior half of the germarium (shown in different z-sections in E') were still labeled at 60 hr APF
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 2E showing occasional EdU incorporation in anterior ICs.

claim: By 96 hr APF, EdU labeling was confined to more posterior cells.
source: before (F) EdU labeling was confined to more posterior cells by 96 hr APF.
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 2F showing the spatial restriction of EdU incorporation.

claim: Most clones initiated 4–6d before eclosion contained only ECs or FSCs together with ECs, indicating a common precursor.
source: (B) Most clones initiated 4–6d before eclosion contained only ECs (blue) or FSCs together with ECs (red), indicating a common precursor.
evidence: This is a primary finding from lineage tracing experiments shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Clones containing only ECs declined and clones containing FSCs but no ECs increased in frequency when initiated at later times.
source: Clones containing only ECs declined and clones containing FSCs but no ECs (green) increased in frequency when initiated at later times.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Of clones containing r1 ECs, inclusion of other r1 ECs was the most frequent, and r2a ECs were more commonly included than more distant FSCs.
source: (C) Clones containing r1 ECs (n = 174) were grouped according to the additional cell types they contained; inclusion of other r1 ECs was the most frequent, and r2a ECs were more commonly included than more distant FSCs.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of lineage data shown in Figure 2C, demonstrating AP clustering.

claim: Clones containing FSCs contained r2a ECs more frequently than r1 ECs.
source: (D) Clones containing FSCs (n = 155) contained r2a ECs more frequently than r1 ECs.
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of lineage data shown in Figure 2D, demonstrating AP clustering.

claim: Marked lineages were clustered along the AP axis, with larger clones towards the posterior.
source: Marked lineages were clustered along the AP axis, with larger clones towards the posterior, suggesting limited AP dispersion and an AP gradient of proliferation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lineage data showing AP clustering and clone size variation.

claim: FSC lineages almost always included marked FCs and mostly included ECs, especially if initiated early.
source: FSC lineages almost always included marked FCs and mostly included ECs, especially if initiated early, indicating that specific stem cell precursors are not determined early
evidence: This is a summary of lineage data showing that FSC precursors are not specified early.

claim: FSCs likely simply acquire their characteristics according to AP location at the end of pupal development.
source: instead, FSCs likely simply acquire their characteristics according to AP location at the end of pupal development.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lineage data showing gradual fate acquisition based on position.

claim: ECs and FSCs, as well as some FCs, derive from intermingled cell (IC) precursors that are interspersed with germline cells throughout pupal development.
source: Combined lineage and morphological studies showed that ECs and FSCs, as well as some FCs, derive from intermingled cell (IC) precursors that are interspersed with germline cells throughout pupal development
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from combining lineage tracing and morphological observations.

claim: An expanding population of cells posterior to ICs become the FCs of the first-formed egg chamber.
source: while an expanding population of cells posterior to ICs become the FCs of the first-formed egg chamber.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from lineage tracing and morphological observations of EGC and basal stalk cells.

claim: The first pupal egg chamber is formed by migration of a germline cyst out of the developing germarium into an accumulation of future FCs.
source: Live imaging showed that the first pupal egg chamber is formed by migration of a germline cyst out of the developing germarium into an accumulation of future FCs, contrasting with the emergence of an FC-encased germline from the germarium that characterizes adult egg chamber budding.
evidence: This is a primary finding from live imaging experiments showing a distinct mechanism for first egg chamber formation.

claim: Stem cells arise from precursors that also build the niche and the adult tissue they support.
source: They arise from precursors that also build the niche and the adult tissue they support.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the collective lineage and morphological data.

claim: The use of delayed specification and shared precursors, together with an evolving spatial gradient of proliferation, may be an effective general developmental strategy to juxtapose and produce appropriate numbers of stem and niche cells in the adult tissue.
source: The use of delayed specification and shared precursors, together with an evolving spatial gradient of proliferation, may be an effective general developmental strategy to juxtapose and produce appropriate numbers of stem and niche cells in the adult tissue.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion about the general significance of the findings.

claim: By the end of the third larval instar, each ovary has 15–20 anterior stacks of non-dividing TF cells.
source: By the end of the third larval instar, each ovary has 15–20 anterior stacks of non-dividing TF cells (Figure 1A and B), which express Lamin-C but not Traffic Jam (TJ) (cyan arrowheads in Figure 1C and E–G; Godt and Laski, 1995; Panchal et al., 2017; Sahut-Barnola et al., 1996).
evidence: This is a direct observation supported by Figure 1 and citations to prior work.

claim: About six somatic cells surround the most posterior TF cell, the transition cell, and become non-dividing cap cells.
source: About six of these somatic cells surround the most posterior TF cell, the transition cell, and become non-dividing cap cells, which express Lamin-C and TJ, shortly after the larval/pupal transition in response to Notch signaling and an ecdysone pulse (Panchal et al., 2017; Gancz and Gilboa, 2013; Gancz et al., 2011; Song et al., 2007; Yatsenko and Shcherbata, 2018; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: PGCs that contact cap cells largely remain in position to become adult GSCs.
source: Primordial germline cells (PGCs) that contact cap cells largely remain in position to become adult GSCs, supported by local cap cell products, including BMPs and Perlecan (Diaz-Torres et al., 2021; Asaoka and Lin, 2004; Zhu and Xie, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on GSC specification.

claim: ICs express TJ but not Lamin-C or Fas3 at pupariation.
source: ICs express TJ (white in Figure 1B–J) but not Lamin-C or Fas3 (both red in Figure 1C–J) at pupariation (Gilboa, 2015; Lai et al., 2017; Panchal et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1 supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ICs have been suggested to be the source of adult ECs.
source: ICs have been suggested to be the source of adult ECs (Gilboa, 2015), but neither this relationship nor the source of FSCs and FCs in newly eclosed adults has been clearly defined experimentally.
evidence: This is a statement about prior suggestions in the literature, with a citation.

claim: Posterior PGCs start to express the early differentiation marker, Bam-GFP, just prior to pupariation.
source: Posterior PGCs start to express the early differentiation marker, Bam-GFP, just prior to pupariation, coincident with a strong ecdysone pulse (Gancz et al., 2011; Zhu and Xie, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on germline differentiation.

claim: Branched fusomes are seen shortly after pupariation, indicating divisions with incomplete cytokinesis to form cysts with two or more cells.
source: Branched fusomes are seen shortly afterwards, indicating divisions with incomplete cytokinesis to form cysts with two or more cells (Li et al., 2019; Gancz et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and observations in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: We observed 2 cell cysts at 0 hr APF, cysts of up to 8 cells by 12 hr APF, and 16 cell cysts at 18 hr APF.
source: We observed 2 cell cysts at 0 hr APF, cysts of up to 8 cells by 12 hr APF, and 16 cell cysts at 18 hr APF (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C showing germline cyst progression.

claim: Progressively larger cysts were arranged, with few exceptions, from anterior to posterior from 18 hr APF onward.
source: Progressively larger cysts were arranged, with few exceptions, from anterior to posterior from 18 hr APF onward; this was particularly clear in samples from 24 to 48 hr APF (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 1D-F showing spatial organization of germline cysts.

claim: EdU labeling was often seen in the most posterior cyst(s) up to 24 hr but rarely at 36 hr.
source: Consistent with these observations of cyst progression and location, EdU labeling was often seen in the most posterior cyst(s) up to 24 hr but rarely at 36 hr, while at 48 hr even the second most posterior cyst in the germarium rarely incorporated EdU (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-D showing EdU incorporation patterns.

claim: Our observations reveal a progression of germline differentiation from single cells to 16 cell cysts that is spatially organized along the AP axis during the first 48 hr APF.
source: Our observations reveal a progression of germline differentiation from single cells to 16 cell cysts that is spatially organized along the AP axis during the first 48 hr APF; at 48 hr APF, the organization of germline cysts resembles that in the adult up to a stage 2b cyst (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the germline development observations.

claim: In the first set of lineage experiments, we dissected ovarioles from adults 2d after eclosion, having induced MARCM clones daily between 6d and 2d before eclosion.
source: We principally used MARCM clonal analysis (Lee and Luo, 2001) because positive cell marking with GFP greatly facilitates scoring all cells in a lineage. However, maturation of a strong GFP MARCM signal in adult and developing ovarioles requires almost 4d. We therefore dissected ovarioles from adults 2d after eclosion ('+2d') in our first experiments, having induced clones daily (in separate samples) between 6d and 2d before eclosion ('–6d' to '–2d'; Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the experimental design for the first set of lineage experiments.

claim: The average number of labeled ECs and FSCs in a marked adult germarium decreased when clones were induced at progressively later stages.
source: The average number of labeled ECs and FSCs in a marked adult germarium decreased when clones were induced at progressively later stages (from an average of 8.1 at –6d to 2.0 at –2d), consistent with proliferation of most precursors during this period (Tables 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the lineage data in Tables 1 and 2.

claim: TF cells were almost never labeled and cap cell labeling was seen only at the earliest times of induction.
source: As expected, TF cells were almost never labeled and cap cell labeling was seen only at the earliest times of induction (present in 3% of clones induced at –5d [0 hr APF]) because these non-dividing cell types have already differentiated shortly before (TFs), or just after (CCs) the larval/pupal transition and the MARCM method only labels dividing cells.
evidence: This is an observation from the lineage data, with an explanation based on known biology of TF and cap cells.

claim: Almost all ovarioles with early-induced clones (from –6d to –4d) that included marked FSCs also contained marked ECs.
source: Strikingly, almost all ovarioles with early-induced clones (from –6d to –4d) that included marked FSCs also contained marked ECs ('EC/FSC clones') (Figure 2B, G and H; Table 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the lineage data shown in Figure 2B and Table 1.

claim: Ovarioles containing only marked ECs were seen at each time of clone induction.
source: Ovarioles containing only marked ECs ('EC only') were seen at each time of clone induction (Figure 2B, E, F, I, J)
evidence: This is a direct observation from the lineage data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A significant frequency of ovarioles with marked FSCs but no marked ECs was evident only when induced at 48 hr or 72 hr APF.
source: while a significant frequency of ovarioles with marked FSCs but no marked ECs ('FSC only') was evident only when induced at 48 hr or 72 hr APF (Figure 2B and L).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the lineage data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: These observations immediately suggested that most adult FSCs derive from a dividing precursor that gives rise to both ECs and FSCs.
source: These observations immediately suggested that most adult FSCs derive from a dividing precursor that gives rise to both ECs and FSCs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lineage data showing frequent co-occurrence of ECs and FSCs in clones.

claim: During the second half of pupation, an increasing proportion of the products of early EC/FSC precursors produce FSCs but no ECs.
source: During the second half of pupation, an increasing proportion of the products of early EC/FSC precursors produce FSCs but no ECs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the increasing frequency of FSC-only clones at later times of induction.

claim: The marked cells in an adult germarium were generally clustered in the AP dimension.
source: The marked cells in an adult germarium were generally clustered in the AP dimension (Figure 2E–L).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the lineage data shown in Figure 2E-L.

claim: Of all early-induced clones with two or more marked cells and including at least one r1 EC, 35% contained only r1 ECs, 19% included also only r2a ECs, while only 8% also included only FSCs.
source: Of all early-induced clones (–6d to –4d) with two or more marked cells and including at least one r1 EC, 35% contained only r1 ECs, 19% included also only r2a ECs, while only 8% also included only FSCs (the remainder included both r2a ECs and FSCs; Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the lineage data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Genetic relatives of a marked region 1 EC are often only in region 1; they are also more commonly found in region 2a than in the more distant FSC region.
source: Thus, genetic relatives of a marked region 1 EC are often only in region 1; they are also more commonly found in region 2a than in the more distant FSC region, even though the total frequency of clones with marked region 2a ECs (54%) and FSCs (57%) were similar (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the quantitative analysis in Figure 2C showing AP clustering.

claim: Of all clones with two or more marked cells including at least one FSC, 25% contained no ECs, 18% included also only r2a ECs, while only 11% also included only r1 ECs.
source: Conversely, of all clones with two or more marked cells including at least one FSC, 25% contained no ECs, 18% included also only r2a ECs, while only 11% also included only r1 ECs, even though the total frequency of clones with r1 ECs (68%) was higher than for r2a ECs (54%) (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis of the lineage data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Precursors occupy significantly different AP positions early in pupal development.
source: These observations suggest that (i) precursors occupy significantly different AP positions early in pupal development
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the AP clustering of marked cells in lineages.

claim: Precursor progeny undergo stochastic movement in either direction but still remain relatively close in the AP dimension.
source: (ii) their progeny undergo stochastic movement in either direction but still remain relatively close in the AP dimension
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the AP clustering patterns and overlap of lineages.

claim: Cell identity (r1 EC, r2a EC or FSC) is set by their AP location at eclosion.
source: and (iii) cell identity (r1 EC, r2a EC or FSC) is set by their AP location at eclosion.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lineage data showing that fate correlates with position rather than lineage.

claim: GFP-only clones, induced at 0 hr APF and scored in newly eclosed adults, were found at an overall frequency of 26/115 ovarioles.
source: GFP-only clones, induced at 0 hr APF and scored in newly eclosed (0d) adults, were found at an overall frequency of 26/115 ovarioles, so that an estimated 86% of labeled ovarioles (see Materials and methods) might be expected to have lineages derived from a single GFP-only cell.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the multicolor lineage experiment.

claim: Among GFP-only lineages that included FSCs, eight also included ECs and only two did not.
source: Among GFP-only lineages that included FSCs, eight also included ECs (Figure 3B and C) and only two did not.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the multicolor lineage data shown in Figure 3.

claim: We can be confident that a single precursor at –5d (0 hr APF) can give rise to both ECs and FSCs and that most FSCs originate from such precursors.
source: We can therefore be confident that a single precursor at –5d (0 hr APF) can give rise to both ECs and FSCs and that most FSCs originate from such precursors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the multicolor lineage data showing high frequency of EC/FSC clones.

claim: Lineages of different colors in the same germarium were generally offset along the AP axis.
source: Lineages of different colors in the same germarium were generally offset along the AP axis, presumably reflecting differences in AP location of the initially marked cell.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the multicolor lineage data shown in Figure 3E-G.

claim: For –6d and –5d samples, the calculated number of ECs made from dividing precursors was very similar at about 33 per germarium.
source: For –6d and –5d samples, the calculated number of ECs made from dividing precursors was very similar at about 33 (19 r1 and 14 r2a) per germarium (Table 2).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the lineage data in Table 2.

claim: The calculated number of ECs made from dividing precursors approximates the total number of adult ECs.
source: This approximates the total number of adult ECs, which has been reported to be about 40 on average (Wang and Page-McCaw, 2018), and which we counted as 32–51 over 25 germaria from young adults, suggesting that most cells that will become adult ECs are still dividing at the larval/pupal transition.
evidence: This is an inference drawn by comparing the calculated number to reported and observed EC numbers.

claim: The calculated number of ECs made from dividing precursors dropped slightly in –4d samples and more markedly in –3d and –2d samples.
source: The calculated number of ECs made from dividing precursors dropped slightly in –4d samples (from 33 to 28) and more markedly in –3d (to 15) and –2d samples (to 13) (Table 2).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the lineage data in Table 2.

claim: Precursors of over half of the future adult EC population have ceased dividing by 2–3 days prior to eclosion.
source: We surmise that precursors of over half of the future adult EC population have ceased dividing by 2–3 days prior to eclosion.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the decline in calculated EC numbers from dividing precursors.

claim: The average number of dividing precursors per germarium for r1 ECs was significantly lower than for r2a ECs by –2d (72 hr APF).
source: Moreover, the average number of dividing precursors per germarium for r1 ECs (4.6) was significantly lower than for r2a ECs (8.6) by –2d (72 hr APF), even though adults contain more r1 than r2a ECs (19 vs. 14, from –6d and –5d data).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the lineage data in Table 2.

claim: Cessation of precursor division appears to spread from the anterior towards the posterior as pupal development proceeds.
source: Thus, cessation of precursor division appears to spread from the anterior towards the posterior as pupal development proceeds.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential decline in r1 vs r2a EC precursor numbers.

claim: Most ovarioles with marked FSCs also had marked ECs when clones were induced at 0 hr APF and examined in newly eclosed adults.
source: We first examined lineages induced at 0 hr APF. Most ovarioles with marked FSCs also had marked ECs (24/27) (Figure 4A and D), as observed for MARCM analysis in 2d-old adults and multicolor clone analysis, confirming a common precursor of ECs and FSCs.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the lineage data shown in Figure 4A and D.

claim: Almost all clones with marked FSCs also had marked FCs when induced at 0 hr APF.
source: Almost all clones with marked FSCs also had marked FCs (25/27) (Figure 4A), indicating a common precursor for adult FSCs and FCs.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the lineage data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: A significant proportion of all marked ovarioles (23/98 = 23%) had marked ECs, FSCs, and FCs when clones were induced at 0 hr APF.
source: A significant proportion of all marked ovarioles (23/98 = 23%) had marked ECs, FSCs, and FCs, indicating that some individual pupal precursors give rise to all three cell types in newly eclosed adults.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the lineage data.

claim: At the start of pupation the most anterior precursors produce ECs, the most posterior precursors produce only FCs and precursors in between produce FSCs, mostly together with both ECs and FCs.
source: These results suggest that at the start of pupation the most anterior precursors produce ECs, the most posterior precursors produce only FCs and precursors in between produce FSCs, mostly together with both ECs and FCs (summarized in Figure 5).
evidence: This is a summary inference drawn from the lineage data and illustrated in Figure 5.

claim: The percentage of clones with marked immediate FCs was higher for ovarioles that included marked FSCs than for those without marked FSCs.
source: The percentage of clones with marked immediate FCs was higher for ovarioles that included marked FSCs (56%) than for those without marked FSCs (16%).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the lineage data.

claim: The percentage of ovarioles with marked FCs in at least one of the two terminal egg chambers was higher when marked FSCs were absent than when they were present.
source: Conversely, the percentage of ovarioles with marked FCs in at least one of the two terminal (most posterior) egg chambers was higher when marked FSCs were absent (88%) than when they were present (67%).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the lineage data.

claim: Occupancy by marked FCs decreased gradually from anterior to posterior for FSC/FC clones and with the opposite polarity for FC-only clones.
source: Indeed, occupancy by marked FCs decreased gradually from anterior to posterior for FSC/FC clones and with the opposite polarity for FC-only clones (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the lineage data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Derivatives of a given precursor were clustered along the AP axis in FSC/FC territory.
source: Thus, derivatives of a given precursor were clustered along the AP axis in FSC/FC territory, as previously noted for EC/FSC territory.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the FC distribution patterns in lineages.

claim: The number of precursors at 0 hr APF was deduced to be about 24 in total, with 15.1 precursors giving rise only to ECs, 3.1 precursors producing ECs and FSCs, 1.2 precursors producing FSCs but no ECs, and 4.6 precursors producing only FCs on average.
source: From those numbers, we deduced the number of dividing precursors at pupariation to be about 24 in total, with 15.1 precursors giving rise only to ECs, 3.1 precursors producing ECs and FSCs, 1.2 precursors producing FSCs but no ECs, and 4.6 precursors producing only FCs on average (Figure 4E, Table 3).
evidence: This is a calculation based on modeling the lineage data, shown in Figure 4E and Table 3.

claim: For multicolor GFP-only clones, we deduced that a single precursor cell gives rise to both ECs and FSCs in 25% of all marked lineages.
source: We deduced that a single precursor cell gives rise to both ECs and FSCs in 25% of all marked lineages and that the frequency of such precursors greatly exceeds precursors that produce FSCs but no ECs (10%).
evidence: This is a calculation based on modeling the multicolor lineage data.

claim: The deduced numbers of precursors of each type from multicolor clones are reasonably similar to those calculated for the similarly timed MARCM experiment.
source: The deduced numbers of precursors of each type (9.0 EC, 4.2 EC/FSC, 1.6 FSC, 2.4 FC, and 17 total precursors) are reasonably similar to those calculated for the similarly timed MARCM experiment (Figure 4E, Table 3).
evidence: This is a comparison of calculations from different lineage experiments.

claim: At 36 hr APF, the proportions of single-cell lineage types were estimated as EC-only (51%), EC/FSC(±FC) (7%), FSC(±FC) (4%), FC-only (38%).
source: Nevertheless, we estimated (see Materials and methods) that the proportions of single-cell lineage types were EC-only (51%), EC/FSC(±FC) (7%), FSC(±FC) (4%), FC-only (38%), and that the total number of dividing precursors was about 35 (Figure 4E, Table 3).
evidence: This is a calculation based on modeling the lineage data from clones induced at 36 hr APF.

claim: At 36 hr APF there are between 5 and 18 non-dividing EC precursors.
source: Based on earlier analysis of MARCM lineages induced at –4d and –3d and examined at +2d, there should also be between 5 and 18 non-dividing EC precursors at –3.5d (Table 2).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from earlier lineage data in Table 2.

claim: At 36 hr APF there are 13.3 FC-only precursors within a total precursor population of about 40–53.
source: Thus, we estimate that at 36 hr APF there are 13.3 FC-only precursors within a total precursor population of about 40–53 (35 dividing plus 5–18 non-dividing cells) (Table 3).
evidence: This is a calculation combining dividing and non-dividing precursor estimates.

claim: The most striking difference between lineages induced at 36 hr versus 0 hr APF is a large increase in lineages producing only FCs.
source: The most striking difference between lineages induced at 36 hr versus 0 hr APF is a large increase in lineages producing only FCs.
evidence: This is a comparison of lineage data from different time points.

claim: More than half of FC-only clones induced at 36 hr APF included labeled FCs in the fourth egg chamber.
source: For FC-only clones induced at 36 hr APF, more than half (34 out of 49) included labeled FCs in the fourth (most mature) egg chamber.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the lineage data.

claim: Two-thirds of FC-only clones with marked FCs in egg chamber 4 had no other labeled FCs, showing that many precursors are restricted by 36 hr APF to contribute only to the first-formed egg chamber.
source: Two-thirds of those (21 out of 34) had no other labeled FCs, showing that many precursors are restricted by 36 hr APF to contribute only to the first-formed egg chamber (Figure 6E and F).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the lineage data shown in Figure 6E and F.

claim: The proportion of the egg chamber 4 epithelium occupied by marked FCs was significantly lower when marked FCs were also in egg chamber 3 than when confined to only the terminal egg chamber.
source: We also found that the proportion of the egg chamber 4 epithelium occupied by marked FCs was significantly lower when marked FCs were also in egg chamber 3 (19.6%) than when confined to only the terminal egg chamber (29.7%) (Figure 6B and D).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the lineage data shown in Figure 6B and D.

claim: We estimate that FCs are allocated to egg chamber 4 at about 47–60 hr APF.
source: We do not know the cell cycle time for these FC-only precursors subsequent to 36 hr APF, but we expect (from amplification data for EC/FSC lineages in Table 1) that it is shorter than 24 hr and may be as short as 11 hr, the cycling time for early FCs in adult ovarioles (Margolis and Spradling, 1995), so we estimate that FCs are allocated to egg chamber 4 at about 47–60 hr APF.
evidence: This is an estimate based on cell cycle time assumptions and lineage data.

claim: By 48 hr APF, all germaria have a single cyst in the most posterior region.
source: By 48 hr APF, all germaria have a single cyst in the most posterior region (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Neighboring somatic cells (ICs) only express low levels of Fas3 at 48 hr APF.
source: but neighboring somatic cells (ICs) only express low levels of Fas3 (Figure 1H and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 1H and Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The most posterior ICs that do not express Fas3 strongly before 48 hr APF appear to be far behind schedule to become FCs of the first budded egg chamber.
source: The most posterior ICs that do not express Fas3 strongly before 48 hr APF therefore appear to be far behind schedule, given that the first egg chamber will bud at about 56 hr APF on average (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing IC Fas3 expression to the timing of egg chamber budding.

claim: ICs may not be the cells that become the FCs of the first budded egg chamber.
source: These observations suggest that ICs may not be the cells that become the FCs of the first budded egg chamber, as might have been assumed by analogy to budding of adult egg chambers.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the Fas3 expression timing.

claim: The distribution of marked FCs in lineages initiated at 36 hr APF suggests that precursors of the first-formed egg chamber contribute only to the two terminal egg chambers.
source: The distribution of marked FCs in lineages initiated at 36 hr APF (Figure 6E) suggests that precursors of the first-formed egg chamber contribute only to the two terminal egg chambers (seen in 32/34 cases).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the FC distribution patterns in lineages shown in Figure 6E.

claim: By 36 hr APF the FC-only precursors appear to be segregated into two populations.
source: Thus, by 36 hr APF the FC-only precursors appear to be segregated into two populations. The majority contribute FCs to the first-formed egg chamber and sometimes also to egg chamber 3, while the remainder contribute FCs to more anterior egg chambers, sometimes including egg chamber 3.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the FC distribution patterns in lineages.

claim: At 36 hr APF it appears that more than two-thirds of FC-only precursors will contribute to the first-formed egg chamber.
source: Thus, at 36 hr APF it appears that more than two-thirds of FC-only precursors will contribute to the first-formed egg chamber (with some also contributing to egg chamber 3), while more anterior egg chambers are later populated by derivatives of a combination of FC-only, FSC/FC, and EC/FSC/FC precursors.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lineage data and FC distribution patterns.

claim: Posterior to the interspersed germline cells and somatic ICs of the pupal germarium are somatic cells with strong Fas3 staining from 24 hr APF onward.
source: Posterior to the interspersed germline cells and somatic ICs of the pupal germarium are somatic cells with strong Fas3 staining from 24 hr APF onward (Figures 1 and 7).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figures 1 and 7.

claim: The most anterior Fas3-positive cells express TJ and form a small multilayered cone or crown around the posterior of the developing germarium that increases in size from 12 to 36 hr APF.
source: We noticed that the most anterior of these Fas3-positive cells express TJ, which is also expressed in ICs and required for their interspersion with germline cells (Li et al., 2003). These TJ/Fas3-positive cells form a small multilayered cone or crown around the posterior of the developing germarium that increases in size and cellular content from 12 to 36 hr APF (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 7A-C.

claim: We refer to TJ/Fas3-positive cells beyond the most posterior germline cyst as the EGC.
source: We refer to those TJ/Fas3-positive cells beyond the most posterior germline cyst as the EGC, and to the more posterior Fas3-positive cells with no TJ expression as basal stalk cells.
evidence: This is a definition introduced by the authors based on their observations.

claim: Expression of Fas3 distinguishes adult FCs from other TJ-expressing cells (FSCs and ECs), suggesting that EGC cells may become the first FCs.
source: Expression of Fas3 distinguishes adult FCs from other TJ-expressing cells (FSCs and ECs) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D; Reilein et al., 2017), suggesting that EGC cells may become the first FCs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the Fas3 expression pattern and prior knowledge.

claim: There is no longer a recognizable EGC after two egg chambers have budded.
source: There is no longer a recognizable EGC after two egg chambers have budded, and the two most mature germline cysts are surrounded by strongly Fas3-positive cells within the germarium, as in adults.
evidence: This is a direct observation from morphological analysis.

claim: Budding of the third, and subsequent, egg chamber is likely similar to the process in adults.
source: Budding of the third, and subsequent, egg chamber is therefore likely similar to the process in adults, with cysts emerging from the germarium completely encased by FCs.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the morphological observations.

claim: Precursors of FC-forming ICs were almost certainly resident in the germarium throughout pupation because we never observed cells in the expanding EGC population entering the germarium.
source: Precursors of those FC-forming ICs were almost certainly resident in the germarium throughout pupation because we never observed cells in the expanding EGC population entering the germarium.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from live imaging observations.

claim: FSC precursors must be ICs, residing within the germarium throughout pupation.
source: FSC precursors, which are anterior to FC precursors, must therefore also be ICs, residing within the germarium throughout pupation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the spatial organization of precursors and the observation that EGC cells don't enter the germarium.

claim: Over 60 TJ-positive somatic ICs were seen in the germarium as the first germline cyst leaves the germarium at about 48 hr APF.
source: This important deduction is supported also by consideration of cell numbers. Over 60 TJ-positive somatic ICs were seen in the germarium as the first germline cyst leaves the germarium at about 48 hr APF (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is a direct observation from Figure 7D.

claim: The number of ICs in the germarium at 48 hr APF exceeds the total number of ECs plus FSCs in an adult germarium.
source: This exceeds the total number of ECs (about 40 on average) plus FSCs (about 16) in an adult germarium, even though many of these precursors are still dividing and amplifying towards producing a full complement of adult ECs and FSCs.
evidence: This is a comparison of cell counts to known adult numbers.

claim: The ICs in the germarium at about 48 hr APF must include all EC and FSC precursors, as well as a significant number of FC precursors.
source: Thus, the ICs in the germarium at about 48 hr APF must include all EC and FSC precursors, as well as a significant number of FC precursors.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cell count comparison.

claim: By scoring FSCs directly, counting the number of labeled ECs and FSCs in each sample, and comparing the results to those for heat-shock induced single-cell lineages, we were able to deduce that ovarioles almost always harbored more than one lineage initiated by bond-GAL4.
source: By scoring FSCs directly, counting the number of labeled ECs and FSCs in each sample, and comparing the results to those for heat-shock induced single-cell lineages, we were able to deduce that ovarioles almost always harbored more than one lineage initiated by bond-GAL4.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from analyzing bond-GAL4 lineage data.

claim: Inferred single-cell lineages from bond-GAL4 were very similar to those induced by marking any dividing cell at pupariation.
source: This allowed us to estimate the composition of single-cell lineages, and we found that they were very similar to those induced by marking any dividing cell at pupariation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing bond-GAL4 lineages to MARCM lineages.

claim: In bond-GAL4 lineages, labeled FSCs almost always included labeled ECs, compatible with a common precursor.
source: In those lineages, which appear to be initiated throughout the IC region, rather than specifically in cells posterior to ICs, we found that labeled FSCs almost always included labeled ECs, compatible with a common precursor.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from analyzing bond-GAL4 lineage data.

claim: We found evidence that bond-GAL4 also targets cells that become FCs of the first-formed egg chamber very late in pupal development.
source: We did find evidence that bond-GAL4 also targets cells that become FCs of the first-formed egg chamber very late in pupal development.
evidence: This is a direct observation from bond-GAL4 lineage experiments.

claim: From about 30 hr APF onward, tracked ICs moved short distances relative to other cells in a variety of directions.
source: From about 30 hr APF onward, tracked ICs moved short distances relative to other cells in a variety of directions.
evidence: This is a direct observation from live imaging experiments.

claim: Most ICs maintained their relative AP locations within the developing germarium as cysts moved past them.
source: Most ICs maintained their relative AP locations within the developing germarium as cysts moved past them.
evidence: This is a direct observation from live imaging experiments.

claim: As a cyst moved posterior to contact EGCs, overlying and posterior ICs ended up anterior to the cyst.
source: Similarly, as a cyst moved posterior to contact EGCs (magenta arrow, Figure 8C), overlying and posterior ICs ended up anterior to the cyst (white, yellow, and red arrows, Figure 8C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from live imaging shown in Figure 8C.

claim: These observations support lineage analysis deductions of limited, stochastic precursor movements along the AP axis.
source: These observations support lineage analysis deductions of limited, stochastic precursor movements along the AP axis and suggest that 16 cell germline cysts do not have a stable coating of somatic cells from about 30–50 hr APF.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the live imaging observations.

claim: During the 30–50 hr APF period, there were cell divisions in the EGC and stalk but we saw no evidence of cells moving from the IC region into the EGC or in the reverse direction.
source: During the 30–50 hr APF period, there were cell divisions in the EGC and stalk (Figure 8—video 1) but we saw no evidence of cells moving from the IC region into the EGC or in the reverse direction (see outlined red EGC cells in Figure 8B), suggesting that the EGC population grows primarily as a result of EGC cell division.
evidence: This is a direct observation from live imaging.

claim: The most posterior germline cyst moved out of the germarium into EGC territory as EGC cells enveloped the cyst.
source: The most posterior germline cyst (highlighted by green nuclei in the lower germarium of Figure 9) moved out of the germarium into EGC territory as EGC cells enveloped the cyst.
evidence: This is a direct observation from live imaging shown in Figure 9.

claim: During budding, more posterior EGC cells become associated with the germline cyst exiting the germarium, while more anterior EGCs move past the cyst into the secondary EGC.
source: Thus, during budding, more posterior EGC cells become associated with the germline cyst exiting the germarium, while more anterior EGCs move past the cyst into the secondary EGC, awaiting budding of the next germline cyst.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from tracking individual cells during live imaging.

claim: Even distant basal stalk cells migrated onto the budding germline cyst.
source: Surprisingly, we observed that even distant basal stalk cells migrated onto the budding germline cyst.
evidence: This is a direct observation from live imaging.

claim: Over nearly 15 hr of live imaging the newly budded cyst acquired a set of closely associated cells of epithelial appearance that derived from the EGC and basal stalk cells.
source: Thus, over the nearly 15 hr of live imaging the newly budded cyst acquired a set of closely associated cells of epithelial appearance that derived from the EGC and basal stalk cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from live imaging observations.

claim: During almost 15 hr of viewing from 55 hr APF onward, the number of cells posterior to the budding cyst declined from 32 to 13.
source: During this almost 15 hr viewing period, the number of cells posterior to the cyst declined from 32 to 13 (Figure 9—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from live imaging shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 4C.

claim: Fixed images of later stages, after two egg chambers have budded, revealed an average of nine cells in the stalk posterior to the terminal egg chamber.
source: Fixed images of later stages, after two egg chambers have budded (84 hr APF; Figure 9—figure supplement 4D), revealed an average of nine cells in the stalk posterior to the terminal egg chamber, resembling the structure seen in newly eclosed adults (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from fixed images shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 4D.

claim: Prior to budding, there were 50–65 cells posterior to the germline throughout the time range of 24–48 hr APF.
source: Prior to budding, there were 50–65 cells posterior to the germline throughout the time range of 24–48 hr APF (Figure 9—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from cell counts shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 4A.

claim: When we examined lineages marked at 36 hr APF, we found 13 ovarioles with label in the basal stalk and in FCs of egg chamber 4, suggesting a common origin from basal stalk cells at 36 hr APF.
source: Consistent with this scenario, when we examined lineages marked at 36 hr APF, we found 13 ovarioles with label in the basal stalk and in FCs of egg chamber 4 (Figure 6F and G), suggesting a common origin from basal stalk cells at 36 hr APF.
evidence: This is a direct observation from lineage data shown in Figure 6F and G.

claim: There were 18 ovarioles where FCs in egg chamber 4 were marked but the adult basal stalk was not, consistent with an origin from EGC or anterior basal stalk cells at 36 hr APF.
source: There were 18 ovarioles where FCs in egg chamber 4 were marked but the adult basal stalk was not, consistent with an origin from EGC or anterior basal stalk cells at 36 hr APF (Figure 6E and H–J).
evidence: This is a direct observation from lineage data shown in Figure 6E and H-J.

claim: Live imaging, together with lineage analysis initiated at 36 hr APF, revealed a separate group of FC-only precursors, now identified as basal stalk and EGC cells posterior to the germarium, that become FCs of the first-formed egg chamber.
source: In summary, live imaging, together with lineage analysis initiated at 36 hr APF, revealed a separate group of FC-only precursors, now identified as basal stalk and EGC cells posterior to the germarium, that become FCs of the first-formed egg chamber and contribute also to the second-formed egg chamber.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from combining live imaging and lineage data.

claim: The FC-only precursors that produce FCs anterior to egg chamber 3 must reside within the germarium, as ICs, throughout pupal development.
source: Thus, the FC-only precursors that produce FCs anterior to egg chamber 3, and even more certainly, all precursors of FSCs, which are anterior to FC-only precursors, must reside within the germarium, as ICs, throughout pupal development.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lineage data and live imaging observations.

claim: The frequency of clones producing only ECs fell from 58% and 57% (0 hr and 24 hr APF) to 30% (48 hr APF) and then 14% (72 hr APF).
source: The frequency of clones producing only ECs fell from 58% and 57% (0 hr and 24 hr APF) to 30% (48 hr APF) and then 14% (72 hr APF) (Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the lineage data in Table 1.

claim: The yield of r1 ECs relative to r2a ECs declined from 2.2 (0 hr APF) and 2.6 (24 hr APF) to 0.9 (48 hr APF) and 0.8 (72 hr APF).
source: Moreover, the yield of r1 ECs relative to r2a ECs declined from 2.2 (0 hr APF) and 2.6 (24 hr APF) to 0.9 (48 hr APF) and 0.8 (72 hr APF).
evidence: This is a calculation based on the lineage data in Table 1.

claim: The yield of marked cells per EC/FSC precursor was consistently higher than for more anterior EC-only precursors at all times of clone induction.
source: The yield of marked cells per EC/FSC precursor was also consistently higher than for more anterior EC-only precursors at all times of clone induction, even though the many FCs produced by EC/FSC precursors were not included (Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the lineage data in Table 1.

claim: From 0 to 24 hr APF, ICs throughout the germarium often incorporated EdU.
source: From 0 to 24 hr APF, ICs throughout the germarium often incorporated EdU (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from EdU labeling shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: By 48 hr APF, the prevalence of anterior EdU-labeled ICs was quite low, whereas EGC cells had frequent EdU signals.
source: By 48 hr APF, the prevalence of anterior EdU-labeled ICs was quite low, whereas EGC cells had frequent EdU signals (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is a direct observation from EdU labeling shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: An occasional IC in the anterior half of the germarium could be found with EdU label at 60 hr APF but not at 96 hr APF.
source: An occasional IC in the anterior half of the germarium could be found with EdU label at 60 hr APF but not at 96 hr APF (Figure 1—figure supplement 2E and F).
evidence: This is a direct observation from EdU labeling shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2E and F.

claim: In adult germaria, all r1 ECs express only GFP (FUCCI), indicating G1 (or a G0 state).
